Dear Customers Ordering Shoes,

Please measure your feet as follows to choose the correct shoe size.

A. Foot length
① Place a sheet of white paper on the floor, spread your feet about shoulder-width apart, and stand upright on the paper.
② Use a pencil to mark the farthest point at the tip of your toes (※1) and the farthest point at the back of your heel (※2).
③ Measure the distance between the two points marked with the pencil.

B. Foot circumference
④ Wrap a string around your foot so that it passes over the protruding bones at the base joints of the big toe and little toe (※3).
⑤ Measure the length of the string wrapped around your foot.

（※1）Toe tip: the frontmost part of the foot
（※2）Heel: the back part of the foot
（※3）Base joint: the position closest to where the toe is attached to the rest of the foot

To: Sales Department, Tanaka Motors

Ginzaya Co., Ltd.
Sales Department — Chikara Yamada

Thank you for your continued support.
Thank you very much for recently sending us the promotional pamphlet and price list for your newly released vehicle.

Dear Ms. Mari Yamada,

Regarding the book of yours that I borrowed, I realized only after receiving your letter that I still had not returned it. I am truly very sorry.
I kept your book on a bookshelf so that it would not get dirty, but I can no longer find it. June 10, 2015
Ichiro Tanaka

What kind of gift should you bring when visiting someone’s home?
Basically, it is better to bring something that can be eaten or drunk and leaves nothing behind. Consider the other person’s circumstances when choosing, such as whether they have children or elderly family members, how many people are in the household, and whether anyone has foods they cannot eat. If you bring something like cream cakes, bringing two or three more than the number of family members will usually be appreciated. Also, the shop where you buy the gift should not be near the home of the person you are visiting. Otherwise, they may get a bad impression or suspect that you prepared in a hurry or bought something carelessly just to get it over with.

(※1) Temiyage: A simple gift brought when visiting someone.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai21-sec-p1.vietnamese:
While cooking, a phone call comes in, and the meat or fish burns while the person is talking. Likewise, when someone is studying and a family member speaks to them, they forget what they were thinking about by the time the conversation ends. These phenomena apparently have something to do with a type of memory called "working memory."

According to a book titled "The Science of the Mind and Brain," the brain's memory system "processes" something else, such as a phone call or a conversation with a family member, while "maintaining" the cooking or thoughts being considered during study in a state that can be recalled at any time. "Working memory" functions so that this "maintenance" and "processing" can take place smoothly at the same time.

Last year, Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry launched a campaign to collect (※1) used mobile phones that were sitting unused in households. Why do mobile phones need to be collected? It is because mobile phones contain abundant metal resources.

In addition to gold, silver, and copper, rare metals are also used in mobile phones. Since Japan has very little of these metals, they basically have to be imported, but it is entirely possible to extract and recycle them from mobile phones that are no longer in use. default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai26-sec-p1.vietnamese:
NOTICE REGARDING PET-KEEPING RULES IN THE APARTMENT COMPLEX

There are restrictions on the types of animals that may be kept in this apartment complex. Residents who are moving in with an animal or plan to keep one in the future are asked to follow the rules below.

1. Animals that may be kept in this apartment complex:
In addition to dogs and cats, rabbits, hamsters (※1), small birds, turtles, fish, and so on are permitted.
★ Dangerous animals, such as snakes (※2), are not permitted, even if they are small.

2. Size of dogs and cats:
They must be small enough for one adult to hold in their arms and weigh no more than 10 kg.

3. Number of dogs and cats permitted:
Each household (※3) may keep only one animal, either a dog or a cat.

4. Size and number of small animals other than dogs and cats:
・Small animals other than dogs and cats must be small enough to be kept in a container, such as a cage or hutch, that one person can carry alone.
・Each household may have only one container.
・There is no special limit on the number of animals as long as they can all fit in that container.

5. Households that keep a dog or cat:
They must join the apartment complex’s Pet Club.

Apartment Building Management Board

(※1) Hamster: The name of an animal
(※2) Snake: The name of an animal
(※3) Household (戸): A counter for houses or apartments

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai27-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Notice: ～Please Clean Your Electrical Outlets～

Recently, one previously unexplained cause of fires has been identified. It is a phenomenon called tracking, which occurs between an electrical outlet and the plug (※1) inserted into it.
This phenomenon occurs when a plug is left inserted in an outlet for a long time. Dust gradually accumulates in the gap between the plug and the outlet, and moisture then affects the dust. The area between the two metal prongs (※2) of the plug gradually becomes scorched (※3), reportedly forming an electrical path, or track. Before long, a large electric current flows through this path, causing a fire.
In daily life, we often leave plugs inserted in outlets, and dust in this area is difficult to see, so it can accumulate without our noticing. Please remember to clean the gap between plugs and wall outlets regularly as well.

Apartment Management Office

(※1) Plug: The name of an electrical device inserted into an outlet
(※2) Metal prong: A term for one part of a device, especially referring to a thin metal piece
(※3) Scorched: Burned black by fire

In the automotive industry, which demands new technology every day, a technology recently developed successfully by a Japanese automaker has attracted attention. It is a device that automatically applies the brakes when there is a risk of colliding with a vehicle behind while changing lanes or reversing.
Before this new technology, collision-avoidance technologies for the front and sides had already been put into practical use. These were two technologies: one automatically applies the brakes when a collision with a vehicle ahead is imminent, and the other returns the vehicle to its original lane when it is about to cross the lane markings and collide with a vehicle beside it. It seems that this latest technology has completed a system that helps avoid collisions in every direction—front, rear, left, and right.
Thinking that the fear of collisions will be reduced and that people will be able to drive with greater peace of mind, I, as a poor driver, find this new technology truly valuable.

(From the “News” section of Nissan Motor Co., Ltd.'s website, July 2010
http://www.nissan-global.com/JP/NEWS/2008/)

(※1) Automaker: a company that manufactures automobiles
(※2) Lane: a section of road designated for vehicles by painted lines
(※3) Reverse: to move backward

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai3-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Since ancient times, Japan has had a custom called 「Mushiboshi」 (airing clothes to prevent mold). This practice removes moisture from kimono and protects them from insects, mold, and other threats. It is usually carried out from the end of July, when the rainy season ends, until early August. This is because kimono absorb and retain moisture during the rainy season.
After two or three consecutive sunny days, the kimono are placed in a well-ventilated room from 10 a.m. until around 3 p.m. During this time, people also check whether any parts have become soiled.
Although this custom has rarely been seen in recent years, I think it may still be useful for modern clothing as a practical way of caring for clothes suited to Japan’s climate.

(※1) Moisture: Water contained in objects or air. It cannot be seen with the naked eye.
(※2) Mold: Extremely tiny organisms that grow on food or clothing in places with high temperatures and humidity.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai30-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Besides its natural sweetness, honey has long been enjoyed as a food with medicinal benefits. Compared with sugar, it is 30% sweeter yet contains 20% fewer calories. Because it is digested and absorbed quickly and immediately converted into energy, honey is very beneficial for recovering one's strength after exercise or illness. In addition, honey has extremely strong antibacterial properties and can be expected to help treat and prevent disease. This is why honey is regarded as a leading health food.

The aroma and sweetness of honey vary depending on the flowers from which the bees collect nectar. I like honey made from the flowers of fruit trees or other woody plants. Citrus blossom honey has a sweet-and-sour taste and a fresh aroma. It is especially delicious in coffee or black tea. Among the flowers of woody plants, I like chestnut blossoms. Chestnut blossom honey has an aroma reminiscent of roasted chestnuts. It seems to be particularly suitable for meat dishes.

One important point to note about honey is that it should not be given to infants under one year old. This is apparently because ordinary honey is not sterilized by high-temperature heating, so harmful bacteria may remain in it and endanger young children.

(※1) Honey: A sweet food made by bees from nectar collected from flowers.
(※2) Antibacterial action: The destruction of bacteria (extremely small organisms that cause disease or spoilage).
(※3) Treatment: Curing an illness or injury with medicine, surgery, or other means.
(※4) Chestnut: A type of tree whose fruit or nuts are edible.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai31-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Sometimes a rainbow appears in the sky after the rain stops. The reason rainbows feel so captivating is that they resemble a huge painting drawn across the sky, display a beautiful harmony of colors, and disappear quickly. Because they are often seen in summer, they have become a seasonal word representing summer in haiku poetry.
A rainbow occurs when raindrops act like lenses and separate sunlight into many colors. In addition, small rainbows can be seen beneath large waterfalls or where water sprays into fine droplets from a spray nozzle, when sunlight shines on them. In Japan, a rainbow is said to have 7 colors, but apparently it had only 5 colors in ancient times. In Okinawa, it has 2 colors, so the number of colors seems to differ depending on the region and era.
The kanji「虹」(rainbow) is made up of「虫」(insect) and「工」(craft), supposedly because in China—the place where the kanji was created—people once believed that a rainbow was a snake (※1) or a dragon (※2). Moreover, they said it was a male dragon (※3). I can understand seeing a rainbow stretching across the sky and imagining it as a dragon, but I do not have enough imagination to look at a rainbow and think of a male dragon.

(※1) Snake: the name of an animal
(※2) Dragon: the name of an imaginary animal
(※3) Male: the term for the male sex of an animal

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai32-sec-p1.vietnamese:
It has been ten years since I began using email on my mobile phone. At first, I did not know how to phrase things, so I wrote emails like handwritten letters. At the beginning, I typed expressions such as “Dear Mr. ~” and “Dear ~,” while at the end I used letter-closing expressions such as “Sincerely” and “Thank you in advance.” I think many of the emails I received at that time were like that too.
However, my email style recently began with “Thank you for your email,” and the closing gradually changed to “See you.” I also feel that the emails I receive increasingly contain more conversational expressions than before. When it comes to young people’s emails, they also frequently use emojis and text-based icons, which can be rather difficult, but deciphering them has its own kind of fun.
In this way, email is becoming an increasingly convenient tool that we can use casually. Even if our handwriting is poor, we no longer have to worry about it at all. However, writing a careful handwritten letter is gradually becoming troublesome, and I feel that this is something to be concerned about. I think that the ability to carefully write down by hand what we want to communicate is something we should not want to lose.

This is health information from the 〇〇 City Health Management Office.

◎ Eye health
　Recently, among people visiting hospitals because something feels wrong with their eyes, many have a symptom called ① “corneal abrasion” (*1). This is a condition in which the “corneal epithelium,” the outermost layer of the part of the eye called the iris (*2), is damaged, scratched, or peeled away by some form of irritation. In the past, this condition was commonly seen among contact lens users (*3), but recently it has also been increasing among people who use computers for long periods.
　Watching television also means looking at a screen (*4), just as when using a computer, but this symptom rarely occurs with television. There is a major difference between television and computers. When working on a computer, people stare at the screen for long periods, which reduces the number of times they blink (*5). Blinking helps produce tears that protect the eyes, but when blinking decreases, the surface of the eye becomes dry and much more susceptible to scratches. Many people think their eyes are merely a little tired and rub them with their hands, but this is precisely what they should avoid most. At such times, it is best to consciously ①[blink].
　The condition can also occur for reasons other than fatigue—for example, when the edge of a sheet of paper brushes against the eye, a branch in the garden snaps into the eye, or a baby's fingernail hits the eye.
　If you experience symptoms such as a gritty feeling as though there is dust in your eye, sensitivity to light that makes it difficult to open your eyes, or excessive tearing, visit a hospital and consult a doctor.
　You can also view this health information on a computer. (http://www......)

(*1) Symptom: a condition caused by an illness or injury
(*2) Iris: the colored part of the eye
(*3) Contact lens: a lens placed directly on the eye
(*4) Screen: the surface on which images and text are displayed on a television or computer
(*5) Blink: the momentary movement of closing and opening the eyes

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai38-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Yesterday, the National Fisheries Research Institute announced that it had succeeded in completely closed-cycle aquaculture of eels (※1). Ordinary aquaculture means artificially raising or breeding fish, while complete aquaculture means creating a cycle (※3): raising newly hatched young fish (※2) from artificially produced eggs until they become parent fish, then hatching the eggs produced by those parent fish and raising the young fish again.

Japanese people eat eel very often, but for a long time it was a mystery where eels were born, grew up, and died. However, this was clarified two years ago through university research, which found that eels are born in the western North Pacific, thousands of kilometers from Japan.

The eels we eat today are raised from glass eels caught after they swim thousands of kilometers to Japan. The number of these glass eels has recently declined sharply.

Cheap imported eels have also begun to be sold widely in supermarkets, but many consumers still actively seek eels produced in Japan. It had been said that complete aquaculture was absolutely necessary to ensure a stable supply of eel.

Eight years ago, researchers succeeded in raising glass eels from eggs. This time, those glass eels became parent fish and laid eggs, and those eggs hatched and are continuing to grow. This is ①the first such success in the world.
Against the backdrop of declining wild eel populations, this shows that eels can be reproduced without depending on wild eels.

（Reference: National Fisheries Research Institute website, July 2010
http://www.fra.affrc.go.jp/pressrelease/pr22/2204082/）

(※2) Hatch: For a young fish, bird, or other animal to emerge from an egg

Report on Financial Support from Parents in Married Households

According to the Consumer Lifestyle Panel Survey compiled and published on the 21st by the Institute for Household Economic Research under the Consumer Affairs Agency, among married households, the percentage receiving financial support from the wife’s parents has risen and surpassed the percentage receiving support from the husband’s parents.
The institute stated that “the importance of the wife’s parents, who provide solid support, particularly in raising children, is increasing.”
According to the survey, the percentage of households receiving financial support only from the wife’s parents was 10.4% in 2008, up from 6.1% in the 1998 survey. In contrast, the percentage receiving support only from the husband’s parents was 9.2%, down from 14.1% in 1998.
The percentage of households receiving support from both sets of parents rose from 2.8% to 5%. The majority were households that received no financial support, accounting for 75.4% in the 2008 survey. Among households receiving support only from the wife’s parents, the most common use was for children, such as education expenses, at 60.0%. Married households are strengthening ①[their ties with the wife’s parents through their children].
Among households receiving support only from the husband’s parents, living expenses accounted for the largest proportion, at 50.0%. The average monthly amount of support was 31,000 yen from the wife’s parents alone and 43,000 yen from the husband’s parents alone.
The survey was conducted in October 2008. A total of 576 women aged 25 to 35 responded to the survey on financial support.

(Excerpted from the October 22, 2009 morning edition of the Chunichi Shimbun)

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai40-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Have you ever watched a television commercial and felt that a product advertised by an actor who appeared serious must be trustworthy? Have you also ever thought that students at a university considered difficult to enter must be socially capable as well as academically strong?
　However, a product is not necessarily good simply because it is advertised on television by an actor who appears serious. Nor is a student necessarily socially outstanding simply because they attend a difficult university.
　Nevertheless, when evaluating something, we often overestimate its other qualities if it has one good characteristic. This psychological effect—being influenced by and overestimating a prominent characteristic, or conversely underestimating other aspects—is called the "Halo Effect." The "halo" here refers to the radiant light behind a Buddhist statue.
　Is the reason we carefully style our hair and choose our clothes for an interview not that we think the same kind of thing is happening in the interviewer’s mind? Interviewers should calmly consider whether their impending judgment is being influenced by anything before making an evaluation.

(※1) Television commercial: An advertisement broadcast on television or radio.
(※2) Talent: A person whose main occupation is appearing and working on television or radio.
(※3) Buddhist statue: In Buddhism, an object depicting the form of the Buddha and used as an object of prayer.
(※4) Calmness: A state of thinking and acting in a composed, settled manner.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai41-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Health Center Newsletter

At our center, health examinations are conducted throughout the year. A health examination is useful not only for detecting illness but also as a good opportunity to understand your own health condition and reconsider your lifestyle habits. Please be sure to have regular checkups.

In the "Small Health Lessons" section, beginning this month we will introduce tips for improving lifestyle habits such as diet, sleep, and exercise over six installments. The first installment will focus on "Drinking Alcohol."

Small Health Lesson
~ Drinking Alcohol ~

There is an expression, "being swallowed by alcohol," which means becoming unable to control yourself because you are drunk. This condition negatively affects everyday life. Let us think together about how to drink without being "swallowed by alcohol."
Alcohol, when enjoyed properly, can help both the mind and body relax and allow us to spend an enjoyable time. Here are some ways to enjoy yourself without becoming drunk and losing self-control: First, enjoy your drinks while talking and laughing with family or friends. This helps relieve stress. Next, eat while you drink. Drinking alcohol alone is very hard on the stomach; adding delicious food makes the experience even better. Finally, drink slowly. Drinking quickly will make your body tired. "Eat slowly and laugh happily" while enjoying alcohol—that is the smart way to make friends and stay in control of your drinking.

At the center, we are always available to provide advice about health and lifestyle habits.
The next installment of "Small Health Lessons" will cover the topic of "Diet."

(※1) Reconsider (見直す): To look at or review something again
(※2) Regularly (定期的に): At fixed, specified intervals
(※3) Sleep (睡眠): The act of sleeping
(※4) Stress (ストレス): Something harmful to the mind or body

Notice: 「Energy Festival」

In City 〇〇, the 「Energy Festival」 will be held for one week during Golden Week (April 29 to May 5). This event is an opportunity to learn about 「solar power generation」—producing electricity by harnessing the sun's energy—and to think about energy-related issues.
Solar energy has advantages such as never running out, causing no air pollution, being free, and being available anywhere on Earth. It is an energy source that does not emit CO2 (carbon dioxide), the primary cause of global warming, which is a pressing issue today. At this festival, visitors can experience how solar energy is useful in everyday life through models such as houses equipped with solar power generators and electric cars.
The government has also announced a policy to promote solar power generation, with the goal of increasing its use tenfold over the current level after 10 years (in 2020), and fortyfold by 2030. In addition, the government provides financial assistance to people who purchase solar power generation equipment.
Families are warmly invited to attend this event, which is a good opportunity for children to think about the environment in Japan and around the Earth.
Date: April 29 ～ May 5
Hours: 10:00 ～ 16:00
Location: The square in front of City Hall

《Electric Car Driving Experience》
Every day: ① 12:00 ② 13:00 ③ 14:00 ④ 15:00
(Each session lasts 5 minutes; limited to the first 10 people for each session.)
※ Please do not drive your own car to the venue. Please use a bus or bicycle.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai43-sec-p1.vietnamese:
The 「Consumer Accident Information Database (DB)」, intended to centrally manage online information about consumer-related accidents—such as accidents caused by familiar household electrical appliances, playground equipment, or foreign objects mixed into food—will officially begin operating on April 1. Anyone will be able to search and look up the information from a personal computer. In addition to the Consumer Affairs Agency, the database will involve five ministries: Economy, Trade and Industry; Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism; Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries; Health, Labour and Welfare; and Justice, as well as the National Institute of Technology and Evaluation (NITE) and the National Consumer Affairs Center of Japan... The system has registered approximately 15,000 incidents occurring since last April. When users enter a product name such as "heater" or "bicycle," damage such as "fire" or "burn," or the time of occurrence, a list of accidents will be displayed. [ A - Furthermore ], by clicking on an individual accident, users can view detailed information without revealing personal identities, such as: (1) the date and location of occurrence, (2) the circumstances, and (3) the number of people injured or killed, their ages, and genders. A list of accidents involving the same product or similar circumstances will also be displayed. To help users search quickly, the system also posts a 「Noteworthy Accident Information List」 for cases requiring warnings because incidents of damage have occurred repeatedly, such as "eyelash extensions" and "pressure cookers," or accidents in which children or elderly people were injured or killed. To identify consumers' interests, the system also provides a 「Search Keyword Ranking」 listing the top five keywords.

(Excerpted from the morning edition of the Chunichi Shimbun, March 29, 2010)

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai44-sec-p1.vietnamese:
The festival in the apartment complex where I live is held every year on the evening of the second Sunday in August. There is no singing or dancing stage. There are only a few food stalls and small games that children can play, such as ring toss (※1). However, all the stalls are prepared and operated by the residents’ association (※2).
In the very center of the apartment complex’s plaza stands a large tree, with tables and chairs arranged around it. Adults drink beer while children drink soft drinks or cola, enjoy yakisoba, sausages, grilled chicken skewers, and other foods, and chat with one another.
People do not use cash when shopping at the festival. Before the festival, they exchange cash for vouchers (※3). The vouchers come in only two denominations: 100 yen and 50 yen. Every item is priced so that it can be purchased using 100-yen and 50-yen vouchers. Beer is the most expensive item, costing 200 yen. Customers receive change as well. Parents give young children vouchers worth about 200 or 300 yen, and the children stand in front of the stalls, wondering what to buy. Any leftover vouchers can be exchanged back for cash when the festival ends.
And ①at the end of the festival, there is a much-anticipated prize drawing (※4). Each family receives one ticket. The ticket has two identical sections, one on the left and one on the right. Participants write their house number and name on both sections and tear them apart. One section is put into the drawing box on the day of the festival, while the other is kept for claiming a prize.
The interesting thing about this drawing is that even if you win and your name is called, you cannot receive the prize if you are not there at that moment. Being present does not guarantee that you will win, but if you are absent, there is a 100% chance that you will not receive a prize.

(※1) Ring toss: a recreational game
(※2) Residents’ association: an organization in which residents discuss and resolve their own issues
(※3) Voucher: a coupon that can be used like cash at designated locations
(※4) Drawing: selecting people to receive gifts or prizes

Recently, people often hear the term 「Nakashoku (eating at home with food bought outside)」. Nakashoku is something between eating out at a restaurant and cooking for yourself at home: it means buying prepared food and taking it home to eat.
More and more stores are offering nakashoku. I sometimes use this service myself, and find it extremely convenient when I eat alone. That is because I can buy many different kinds of food, a little of each. Making all these dishes at home would be a great deal of work. To prepare small amounts of different dishes, I would need to prepare all kinds of ingredients. With nakashoku, however, I can save a great deal. I do not need to spend time and effort cooking, nor do I need to prepare many ingredients to make various dishes.
In the past, the main users were single men and working women, but recently this service is said to be expanding to include housewives and elderly people as well. It is very popular among mothers with young children who find it difficult to eat out but want to invite friends to their homes for a meal, as well as elderly people who have difficulty cooking or going out. Some restaurants also deliver prepared meals to their homes.
I often visit nakashoku stores when I get home late from work, and I will probably continue using this service on many different occasions in the future.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai46-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Ever since I was little, I have loved reading manga and often doodled manga-style drawings. I also enjoyed creating stories, so during the early years of elementary school, I drew story-based imitations of manga for fun.
At first, I drew only with a pencil in a notebook. Gradually, I learned that things called manuscript paper and special drawing pens existed, so I bought them and began using them. When I was in middle school, I submitted the works I completed in this way to the manga competition section of a magazine. After submitting several times, in my first year of high school, I was honored to receive an award that qualified me to make my debut, and my career as a professional artist was decided.
It would be inaccurate to say that from the beginning I thought, 'No matter what, I absolutely want to become a manga artist!' I did hope that it would be wonderful if I could become a manga artist, but I never thought I was certain to become one. At that time, I still could not clearly judge whether my potential was developing in any particular direction.
I had not thought deeply about my future, and I also had many wishes besides becoming a manga artist. At one point, I wanted to become a novelist or a children's writer. At another point, I invited friends to practice singing and dancing because I wanted to appear on television like a pop idol. I also thought I might try becoming a film director, cinematographer, or designer. (The rest omitted.)

(From Kitahara Nariko, 'To the Life of a Shōjo Manga Artist,' excerpted from 'Why I Chose This Job,' Iwanami Junior Shinsho Library)

There are many strange words around us. A word like 「Gaijin」(foreigner) is one of them.

Whether you go to the United States or Europe, people there do not call us 「Gaijin」. In my own experience, I have sometimes been asked, 'Are you Japanese?', but I have never been told, 'You're a foreigner, aren't you?' Even if equivalent words to 「Gaijin」 exist, they are used only in extremely special circumstances.

In this country, however, whether they are American, Russian, or Indian, everyone who is not Japanese is called 「Gaijin」. They are labeled 「Gaijin」, lumped together as one group, and viewed with a special attitude whenever anything happens.

Unlike Europe and the United States, where people of many races live intermingled, perhaps in Japan people of other races are still seen as something unusual. As a result, people regard them as 'different-race people' or 'different people' and, somewhere in their minds, try to keep them at a distance.

This is also a form of discrimination. In an age when the Earth is gradually becoming a global village, such an absurd situation cannot be accepted. I think that if this continues, we will gradually become isolated from the rest of the world.

To solve this problem, someone once said, half jokingly and half seriously: 「The best solution is to import 'Gaijin'.」 (The rest of the passage has been omitted.)

(Excerpt from 『What a Fool』 by Yukichi Amano, Chikuma Bunko)

June 15, 2015
Dear Mr. Taro Yamada,

It has been a long time since we last met. I hope you have been keeping well.
Although it was a busy time of year because of rice planting, you and your family treated me like one of the family and welcomed me warmly throughout the past week. I sincerely thank you for taking such good care of me every day.
It was the first time in my life that I had experienced rice planting, and I made many wonderful memories. You taught me a great deal about Japanese agriculture, and thanks to your kindness and help, I was able to decide on a topic for my graduation thesis. Moreover, through my daily conversations with everyone, I gradually became a little more confident in my Japanese. I am truly grateful.
Starting today, classes have resumed. After a week apart, I met my friends again and we talked about our Golden Week holidays. Of course, I told them about the wonderful time I had, including staying with your family, planting rice together, and enjoying Kashiwa-mochi while watching koinobori pray for little Ichiro's healthy growth. One of my juniors, who had just returned to Japan, was extremely envious when he heard my story and said that next year he would definitely apply for a homestay.
From now on, I will use what I learned during my week with your family as I work toward completing my graduation thesis.
I imagine you must be somewhat tired after the rice planting. Please continue to take good care of your health.

I am enclosing a commemorative photograph taken with your family.

Tam Horn

(※1) Golden Week: A long holiday period from late April to early May
(※2) Homestay: A program in which international students or others stay with an ordinary family
(※3) Koinobori: Carp-shaped streamers displayed on Children's Day (May 5)
(※4) Kashiwa-mochi: A Japanese sweet eaten on Children's Day

Ordinary glass breaks easily when dropped or struck by something, whereas tempered glass used in cars and elsewhere is much harder to break. The difference between the two types of glass actually lies in how they are manufactured. Ordinary glass is cooled slowly after the material is heated. During this process, many invisible scratches appear on the surface; when force is applied, the scratches spread and the glass breaks. Tempered glass, on the other hand, is cooled rapidly after being heated, causing the area near the surface to become compressed. As a result, even when force is applied, scratches on the surface are less likely to spread, making the glass harder to break.

（※3）Compress: To apply force so that something contracts or becomes smaller
（※4）Layer: The act of stacking things from top to bottom, or something that has been stacked

Sakura Pedometer User Guide:

Thank you very much for purchasing the Sakura pedometer (※1). Please read the following points carefully before use.

I heard from a friend that a company is about to release a car-navigation device for bicycles. Apparently, the device can guide users not only along major roads but also through narrow streets, and it also provides information about bicycle parking areas and bicycle shops. To the graduates of Midori High School's Heisei 5 graduating class (1993),

It has been a long time since I last contacted you.

It has been 20 years since we graduated from Midori High School. How is everyone doing?

Whether living far from your hometown or working hard at your job, managing your household, or raising children, I am sure that everyone is actively contributing in their own way.

This time, we have planned a class reunion (※1) for the first time in many years. The reason is that Mr. Takahashi published a book last April titled "Thirty Years as an English Teacher," and several classmates immediately expressed their desire to hear him speak. I think it will be extremely interesting for those who are currently teachers and for parents who are concerned about educating their children.

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai71-sec-p1.vietnamese:
Sue plans to graduate from a vocational school next March. She hopes to find work related to healthcare in Japan. She saw the following notice for a joint company information session in a newspaper:

Maiasa Newspaper Job Information Session

【Date and time】October 5 (Tuesday) and October 6 (Wednesday), 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
【Location】Sakura Seimei Hall (5th floor of the Sakura Seimei Building, ○ Street, Chuo Ward, Osaka City)
【Eligibility】People expected to graduate from a university, junior college, or vocational school next March
【Fee】Admission is free. *However, there is a 300-yen fee for materials.
【内容】An event where participants can speak directly with representatives of companies they are interested in, listen to explanations about the work and recruitment exams, and ask questions.
*Appointments cannot be made in advance. On the day of the event, the organizers will provide guidance in the order in which people register at the reception desk.

〈注意〉
◎ An event covering fields such as healthcare and welfare is scheduled for another occasion.
◎ Visitors must bring a résumé on the day of the event.

Maiasa Newspaper Office

(※1) Healthcare: The treatment of illnesses and injuries, as well as the techniques, medicines, and other things used for that purpose
(※2) Welfare: The provision of public services so that everyone can live a happy life
(※3) Résumé: A document recording what a person has studied or worked on up to the present
(※4) Bring along (持参): To bring something with you
to ~ (used at the beginning of letters and notices)
Regarding the common social issue of protecting the global environment, our university, too, would like to put this into practice in daily life, even through small actions.
want to continue doing ~ / want to carry out ~ from now on
For that purpose, please cooperate in carrying out the following items.
in order to do that, for that purpose
1. When you are the last person to leave the classroom, be sure to turn off the lights and air conditioner.
2. Turn on the lights when using places such as restrooms and lounges, and always turn them off after use.
3. Keep the air-conditioner temperature at the standard of 22 degrees in winter and 28 degrees in summer.
4. Do not use a car or motorcycle to commute to school.

The school only requires students not to use cars or motorcycles when commuting; it does not require them to walk. They may use bicycles, buses, trains, and so on. Therefore, choice 1—having to walk to school—is something students do not need to do.
that is all, end of message
the end (used at the end of a formal notice)
expressing possession or association; 私たちの大学 means “our university.”

default.p.n3speeddokkai-bai8-sec-p1.vietnamese:
To all students

Regarding the issue shared by all society of protecting the global environment, our university also wishes to take practical action in daily life, even if the actions are small. For this purpose, please cooperate by following the items below.

1. If you are the last person to leave a classroom, be sure to turn off the lights and air conditioner.
2. In places such as restrooms and lounges, turn on the lights when using them and be sure to turn them off afterward.
3. Set the air conditioner temperature to 22 degrees in winter and 28 degrees in summer.
4. Do not use cars or motorcycles to come to school.

End
Fuji University

(※1) Our university: This university
